name: Spicy Chickpea Stew (Chana Masala) with Cilantro, Cashew & Lime Rice
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, peel and mince garlic and ginger; place in a small bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the garlic and ginger; set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat another medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas in a colander. Set aside to drain further.
Add garlic, ginger, jalapeño, and spices to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 1-2 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Add chickpeas, broth, and diced tomatoes to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until chickpeas are soft and stew has thickened, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop cashews. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place both in the reserved bowl.
Juice one lime into the bowl with the cilantro and cashews. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
When the rice is done, add the cashew-cilantro mixture to the pan and stir to combine; cover and set aside.
When the stew is done, add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Divide rice and chickpea stew between bowls; serve with lime wedges on the side and enjoy!
author: Mealime
